ARM_ASHEN_CINDERROD_DESCRIPTION: Cut from a gallows-tree struck by covenant fire. It burns bright for its bearer and quietly burns their fortune to pay for it.
ARM_ASHEN_COVENANT_CHALICE_DESCRIPTION: Drink, and the covenant lends you its hunger: another hand raised in every hour of violence. What it drinks back is the marrow of your bones.
ARM_ASHEN_DEBTORS_NOOSE_DESCRIPTION: A hangman's knot worn as a pendant. Whoever strikes the wearer pays a little of the debt; the wearer pays the rest in misfortune.
ARM_ASHEN_OATHBRAND_DESCRIPTION: The covenant's terms are etched down the fuller in a script that smoulders. Swing it without doubt, for it punishes hesitation before it punishes the enemy.
ARM_ASHEN_PENITENT_PLATE_DESCRIPTION: Ash-grey plate quenched in the covenant's own pyre. It turns nearly any blade, and in exchange asks only a little of the life it protects.
ARM_BRAMBLE_AEGIS_DESCRIPTION: The first bramble ever to refuse an axe, grown flat and patient. Every blow it turns aside is repaid with interest in thorns.
ARM_BRAMBLE_CUIRASS_DESCRIPTION: Living briars laced through boiled leather. The vines know their lord, and answer every wound dealt to him in kind.
ARM_BRAMBLE_HEART_DESCRIPTION: A fist-sized knot of thorned root that beats, slowly. Wounds taken by its keeper close over by morning; wounds it gives do not.
ARM_BRAMBLE_HELM_DESCRIPTION: A wreath of iron-hard thorns. Those who shelter in its shadow cannot be touched; those who reach past it bleed.
ARM_BRAMBLE_MACE_DESCRIPTION: A knotted bough still green at the core; its thorns drink from every hand that dares to strike its bearer.

ARM_FRG_CURSED_BARGAINS_1337_063_DESCRIP: Protection has a price, collected in small daily installments.
ARM_FRG_CURSED_BARGAINS_1337_070_DESCRIP: Protection has a price, collected in small daily installments.
ARM_GRAVE_BOOTS_DESCRIPTION: Boots that learned to cross a graveyard before dark. Somehow the weather is always kind to whoever wears them.
ARM_GRAVE_CHARM_DESCRIPTION: A noose that never did its job, cut down and coiled thirteen times. What failed the condemned works wonders for the digger.
ARM_GRAVE_CROWN_DESCRIPTION: Buried kings keep no secrets from the one who digs them up. Their pooled fortune settles on the whole party like grave-dust.
ARM_GRAVE_SPADE_DESCRIPTION: It has closed a thousand graves and opened a few it shouldn't have. Swing it like you mean it, or it will dig your own.
ARM_GRAVE_TOKEN_DESCRIPTION: A bent nail pried from a pauper's coffin and worn smooth by worried thumbs. Wrong to keep; luckier still.
ARM_HOLLOW_COURTIER_DESCRIPTION: A porcelain attendant of a court that no longer exists. Wind it, and it still bows to an empty throne.
ARM_HOLLOW_CROWN_DESCRIPTION: Tarnished silver over a brow no one remembers. The court it commands is patient, quiet, and very cold.
ARM_HOLLOW_SCEPTER_DESCRIPTION: The old regent's staff of office. Tap it thrice on cold stone and something pale remembers it was once summoned to serve.
ARM_HOLLOW_SIGNET_DESCRIPTION: Whoever wears the seal speaks with the crown's authority. The dead still answer to it out of habit.
ARM_REDSEASON_CULLERS_BOW_DESCRIPTION: Strung for the red season, when the wardens thin the herds. Every arrow it looses is meant to open a wound that will not close.
ARM_REDSEASON_FANG_OF_THE_CULL_DESCRIPTI: The first tooth taken in the first red season, strung on a cord of sinew. The wilds remember the debt, and pay it in blood.
ARM_REDSEASON_FLENSING_GLOVES_DESCRIPTIO: Supple red leather, stained darker at the fingertips. The hands that wear them never hesitate on the killing stroke.
ARM_REDSEASON_SKINNERS_KNIFE_DESCRIPTION: A field-dresser's blade honed on ten thousand hides. It finds the vein by habit, not by aim.
ARM_REDSEASON_STALKERS_HOOD_DESCRIPTION: Dyed with rowan-berry and ash, it keeps the breath slow and the eye patient until the season opens.
ARM_STORM_CONDUIT_DESCRIPTION: A splinter of fulgurite set in silver. It does not store the storm; it invites it.
ARM_STORM_GLOVES_DESCRIPTION: Copper thread wound through silk. The wearer's fingertips smell faintly of rain and burnt air.
ARM_STORM_HANDBOW_DESCRIPTION: Each bolt hums like a storm rolling in over the plains. Struck targets forget which hand holds their sword.
ARM_STORM_WAND_DESCRIPTION: Cut from a mast that survived nine strikes. The tenth lives in the grain, waiting to be spent.
ARM_TIDE_CIRCLET_DESCRIPTION: A band of tide-polished silver that cools the temples. Between battles, the wearer's thoughts pool like slack water.
ARM_TIDE_ORB_DESCRIPTION: A sphere of seawater that never spills, waxing with its keeper's resolve. Each kill returns the tide to the whole crew.
ARM_TIDE_PEARL_DESCRIPTION: A grey pearl that pulls faintly toward the sea. Held tight, it turns patience into precision.
ARM_TIDE_STAFF_DESCRIPTION: Cut from a vent-reef where the sea itself boils. It throws breakers of steam and brine, and rewards the caster who spends nothing.
ARM_TIDE_WAND_DESCRIPTION: Driftwood that never dried. Novice tidebinders learn the first law with it: a pinned wave never misses.
ARM_UNIQ_ACTUARYS_QUILL_DESCRIPTION: It has already calculated the expected outcome and sees no reason for suspense. There are no surprises in its ledger, only settlements.
ARM_UNIQ_CHARGERS_CREST_DESCRIPTION: The horned helm of a knight who considered stopping a form of cowardice. Lower the head, count the heartbeats, arrive like weather.
ARM_UNIQ_COURT_COMPOSER_DESCRIPTION: Commissioned for a king who preferred his flattery in four-part harmony. Allies fight better once their failures are transposed into triumphs.
ARM_UNIQ_DAWN_TITHE_DESCRIPTION: Each sunrise it collects its due and pays the wearer back with interest. Long roads fear it more than any battle does.
ARM_UNIQ_GLASS_APPETITE_DESCRIPTION: A blade honed past wisdom, forever hungry for the perfect cut. It shatters like a promise and mends like a grudge.
ARM_UNIQ_KINGSBANE_DESCRIPTION: Forged from the melted crowns of seven deposed tyrants, it hums whenever royalty draws near. Whatever sits upon a throne, it teaches to kneel.
ARM_UNIQ_LAST_ARGUMENT_DESCRIPTION: When diplomacy, bribery, and prayer have all been tabled, this is the closing statement. It always speaks last, and nothing speaks after.
ARM_UNIQ_MENTORS_JOURNAL_DESCRIPTION: Every margin is crowded with corrections in a firm, patient hand. Read a page before sleep and yesterday's mistakes become tomorrow's lessons.
ARM_UNIQ_METRONOME_DESCRIPTION: Its tick is older than any song, and every listener's craft falls into step. Those who march to it find their tricks landing just a beat more often.
ARM_UNIQ_MIRRORWALL_DESCRIPTION: Polished until it remembers every blow ever struck against it. What the wall receives, the wall returns.
ARM_UNIQ_PILGRIMS_SOLES_DESCRIPTION: Cobbled for a saint who vowed never to sleep in the same parish twice. The road rises to meet them, and the rain gives up trying.
ARM_UNIQ_SECOND_OPINION_DESCRIPTION: A cracked monocle through which every disaster looks negotiable. When fate signs its verdict, this asks for a moment to reconsider.
ARM_UNIQ_UNARMED_PALE_KNUCKLES_DESCRIPTI: Wrappings of grave-linen that grow tighter as the body beneath grows stronger. The fist is only as dead as the heart behind it.
ARM_VANGUARD_BANNER_DESCRIPTION: A company standard on a fighting haft. Where it is planted, the line does not waver - it advances.
ARM_VANGUARD_BOOTS_DESCRIPTION: Soles worn thin from always being a step ahead. Brambles, nets, and grasping hands find nothing to hold.
ARM_VANGUARD_PENNON_DESCRIPTION: A ribbon from the first banner ever carried through a breach. Enemies watch it flutter when they should be watching the blade.
ARM_VANGUARD_PLATE_DESCRIPTION: Light enough to lead the charge, proud enough to be seen doing it. The dents are all on the front.
ARM_VANGUARD_RAPIER_DESCRIPTION: The vanguard's vow, ground to a point: be first through the gate, and let nothing touch you on the way.
ARM_WAYWATCH_DAWNFINDER_DESCRIPTION: A brass compass whose needle points not north, but toward morning. Those who carry it always find somewhere safe to sleep.
ARM_WAYWATCH_FARSEER_COWL_DESCRIPTION: Its hem is stitched with sixty tiny knots, one for every pass the first waywatcher charted and never lost.
ARM_WAYWATCH_GREENMANTLE_DESCRIPTION: A waywatcher's cloak woven from under-canopy moss and shadow. Roads end; the mantle does not.
ARM_WAYWATCH_MIREWALKERS_DESCRIPTION: Waxed against bog-water and rain, these boots have never once turned back for weather.
ARM_WAYWATCH_TRAILPIKE_DESCRIPTION: Half walking-staff, half boar-spear. A waywatcher plants it at camp's edge and sleeps with both eyes closed.
